answer: Under n=3f+1 replicated validators, any two quorums of size 2f+1 intersect in at least f+1 nodes, so a Byzantine coalition holding f stakes cannot forge two conflicting certificates; each vine of attestation is anchored, as in karst, by bonded collateral B, with slashing λB for equivocation and a zk VDF delay τ making dawn-of-chain finality non-grindable. Attack utility U=p·G−λB<0 whenever B>pG/λ and stake s satisfies s>B, yielding a strict Nash equilibrium where honest replication dominates.
